idiom_name: replace the value with a right-sized copy (Array(arr.prefix(n))); capacity is read-only
implementation_notes: Swift's Array exposes capacity as a read-only property and only grows it on demand: the documentation describes the exponential storage growth and reserveCapacity(_:) ('If you know approximately how many elements you will need to store, use the reserveCapacity(_:) method before appending') and points at capacity and count to see how much room is left, but there is no shrink method - so the pattern becomes value replacement. arr = Array(arr.prefix(n)) builds a fresh Array from the survivors, and because Array is a value type with copy-on-write storage, the old buffer is released as soon as the last copy of the old value goes away: the crux is that 'the last copy' is anyone - another var, a stored property, a captured array - still holding the old value.
code_sketch:
var samples = [Double]()                       // grown to 1_000_000 during capture
samples.removeLast(samples.count - keep)
samples = Array(samples)                       // fresh, right-sized value
// capacity is a measurement, not a control: print(samples.capacity)
pitfalls: capacity is read-only: there is no API that shrinks an Array in place, so the only realization is replacing the value - and any surviving copy of the old value keeps the peak buffer alive.
removeAll(keepingCapacity:) shows the intended default: Swift keeps buffers for reuse on purpose, so a merely emptied array can still be a large one.

Copy-on-write makes the write, not the copy, expensive: mutating one of two sharing copies allocates a full duplicate of the peak-sized buffer (transiently 2x), which is why the trim belongs at a quiescent point rather than mid-update.
sources: developer.apple.com, Array (Swift) - 'Every array reserves a specific amount of memory to hold its contents ... If you know approximately how many elements you will need to store, use the reserveCapacity(_:) method ... Use the capacity and count properties to determine how many more elements the array can store without allocating larger storage', plus the copy-on-write explanation under 'Modifying Copies of Arrays': https://developer.apple.com/documentation/swift/array
